flags.quote: Moving your pawn to e3 is the strongest move because you put more pressure on the center.
flags.critique: This is Van't Kruijs. The eval dropped 25cp and you still called it the strongest move. e3 does not 'put more pressure on the center' than e4 or d4; it is a quieter, slightly worse cousin. 'That's the one.' as a quip makes me think the coach has one volume knob.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to d3 is playable, but moving your pawn to d4 would be better because you can likely take a pawn.
flags.critique: d4 does not take a pawn. It occupies the center and offers a trade after ...exd4. You invented a capture from a continuation and sold it as the reason to play the move. The listed reason is center_control, which is the actual lesson, and you threw it away for a fake tactic.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to c3 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: 45cp gone and zero because-clause. c3 is a useful idea here (prepare d4, bolster the center), and you had backward_pawn sitting in the reasons and did not even try to use it. Calling this strongest with an empty sentence is just a rubber stamp.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to f3 is playable, but moving your f1-bishop to e2 would be better.
flags.critique: f3 is not 'playable' in a way I can learn from. It steals g1 from the knight, pokes holes around the king, and makes e3 look sick. Be2 is suggested with no why. This is the first ugly structural mistake in the game and you shrugged.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to d5 is the strongest move because you put more pressure on the center.
flags.critique: d5 is the actual break against this e3/d3/c3/f3 clump, and you gave me the same center-control sentence as 1.e3. You even tagged backward_pawn and then talked about 'the center' again. Teach the strike, not the Mad Libs slot.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to g3 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: After f3, g3 is a bandage on a kingside you already cut open. No because, no fianchetto, no 'your knight still has no square.' Strongest-plus-silence is not coaching.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to a6 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: Why is a6 the one? Stopping Bb5? Waiting? You had no reasons at all. If you cannot name a plan, do not call a wing pawn nudge the strongest move in the position.

flags.quote: You are still worse, but moving your pawn to b3 gives you a backward pawn. A better move would have been moving your g1-knight to h3.
flags.critique: Which pawn is backward, and what does that word mean on the board? Then you recommend Nh3 like that is obvious. The real story is f3 blocked Nf3, so the knight is homeless — say that. 'Backward pawn' without a file is just a vocab pop quiz.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to h6 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: Another empty strongest. 46cp swing and a 'That's the one.' If this is prophylaxis, name the piece I am not allowing onto g5. Otherwise it is just a tempo I spent on air.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to e4 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: This is the interesting move in the game so far: a wedge into the white pawn mass, cramping d3/f3 and forcing the structure to crack. You said nothing. I would have learned more from a silent board.

flags.quote: Moving your b1-knight to d2 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: 51cp loss is not 'best' under your own thresholds, and the sentence still has no idea. Nd2 develops and maybe prepares to recapture on e4; 'strongest' is a lie born from treating the played move as the engine move.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on d3 with your e-pawn is the strongest move because it leaves you with a passed pawn.
flags.critique: That d3 pawn is hanging on their third rank and they take it back next move with Bxd3. You had hanging in the reasons and still taught me I 'got a passer.' A passed pawn I lose on the spot is not a lesson, it is a bug wearing a phrase-bank line.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on d3 with your f1-bishop is the strongest move because the pawn was undefended.
flags.critique: I recaptured the pawn they just took. That is not winning material; it is not hanging around as a gift. 'Undefended' here is SEE-speak for 'you took back.' king_safer sat unused while you congratulated me for recapturing.

flags.quote: Moving your queen to e2 is the strongest move because it saves your pawn from capture.
flags.critique: e3 is defended by the king and the knight; Bc5 is not winning it. Qe2 is connecting, getting off the d-file, and aiming at 0-0-0. You invented a rescue. Teach the plan, not a hanging-pawn hallucination.

flags.quote: Castling queenside is the strongest move because it gets your king out of danger and activates your rook and it gives your rook a semi-open file.
flags.critique: That sentence is three clauses taped together with 'and.' Opposite-side castling is the whole strategic story of this middlegame — we are going to race — and you talked about a semi-open file without naming the d-file. I noticed the grammar before I noticed a plan.

flags.quote: Moving your d2-knight to f1 is the strongest move because it saves your pawn from capture.
flags.critique: The knight on d2 was a defender of e3. Walking it to f1 does the opposite of saving that pawn. This is a reroute (maybe Ng3/Ne3, maybe unblocking the d-rook). saves_piece fired and you printed a false rescue again.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to d4 puts it at risk of attack from the white pawn and pawn. A better move would have been moving your pawn to a5.
flags.critique: 'The white pawn and pawn' is not English. Name c3 and e3. a5 as the improvement is a queenside poke at the king on c1, and you never said that, so I am left thinking I should have shuffled a rook-pawn for vibes. 158cp is a real mistake; the copy is a broken label printer.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to e4 is a mistake, but taking the pawn on d4 with your c-pawn would be better because the pawn was undefended.
flags.critique: d4 is defended by the knight on c6 and the queen on d8. cxd4 is a capture of a guarded pawn, not a free lunch. You also listed saves_piece on the move I played, which does not appear in the sentence. The real note is: do not push past the tension, take in the center.

flags.quote: Moving your f6-knight to h7 is a mistake, but taking the pawn on c3 with your d-pawn would be better because you can likely pin the pawn to the queen and it unveils an attack from your queen on the white d3-bishop.
flags.critique: Nh7 is a retreat into a hole; dxc3 opening the d-file onto Bd3 is the real idea, and that second half is actually good. The 'likely pin the pawn to the queen' is leftover PV sludge — the e-file pin already exists. 'Likely' plus the wrong tactic is how you teach me not to trust you.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to f5 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: f5 is the break against e4, and you had hanging, backward_pawn, and pawn_shield sitting unused. Empty strongest on a pawn break is malpractice. Tell me I am challenging the center pawn, not that I found 'the one.'

flags.quote: Moving your queen to c2 is playable, but moving your pawn to g4 would be better.
flags.critique: g4 looks like I am opening my own king. If that is the engine move, you owe me a reason (kick f5, grab space, trap a piece). 'Playable' versus a naked g4 is how I ignore the coach on the next ten moves.

flags.quote: Taking the knight on h7 with your e4-bishop is the strongest move because the knight was undefended.
flags.critique: It is check. You tagged check and then dropped it because a capture is 'more tactical.' I just hung a knight last move; the lesson is take the hanging piece with check, not a dry 'undefended' stamp.

flags.quote: Moving your king to h8 is the strongest move because your king is harder to attack.
flags.critique: I walked into the corner next to the bishop that just took on h7. 'Harder to attack' is a king_safer stock line and it does not match the picture. The real choice is Kh8 vs taking on h7 into the queen's diagonal — say that.

flags.quote: Moving your h7-bishop to e4 is a mistake, but moving your pawn to a3 would be better.
flags.critique: You just won a knight with check, then retreated, lost 129cp, and suggested a3 with no reasons. Is a3 stopping Nb4? Is Be4 a tempo loss? I cannot tell. After the only clean tactic in the game, the coach went mute.

flags.quote: Moving your f8-bishop to c5 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: This bishop aims at the king and the e3 pawn. 'Development' is in the reasons and still did not make the sentence. Another strongest with no picture.

suggestions.title: Stop selling PV captures as the move's idea
suggestions.detail: verifyLikelyTactics still lets a 'likely capture/pin' through when eval loss is ≥40 even if the suggested move does not capture. 2.d4 became 'you can likely take a pawn'; 13...dxc3 became 'you can likely pin the pawn to the queen.' Only emit likely capture/pin/fork when the suggested ply itself makes that tactic, or when the first PV ply is that capture. A 1200 hears 'take a pawn' and looks for a capture that is not on the board.

suggestions.title: Do not praise a passer that is hanging
suggestions.detail: ...exd3 was called a passed pawn while hanging was in the reason list and Bxd3 recaptures immediately. In pickBenefitReasons / selectBecauseReasons, drop passed_pawn when that pawn's square is newlyHanging or the recapture is on the next ply of the line. Hanging should outrank a middlegame passer. Otherwise the coach teaches the wrong motif on the most memorable capture of the opening.

suggestions.title: Say undefended only when nothing guards it
suggestions.detail: wins_material copy uses 'the pawn was undefended' when SEE looks good. On 13.e4 the suggested cxd4 is of a pawn guarded by Nc6 and Qd8; Bxd3 is a recapture. Gate that phrase on defender count === 0 (or SEE equal to full piece value with no legal recapture). Recaptures should say you took back, not that you won a hanging unit.

suggestions.title: Fire saves_piece only when a hanging unit becomes safe
suggestions.detail: Qe2 and Nf1 both 'saved your pawn from capture' and both look false: e3 was not hanging on Qe2, and Nf1 walked a defender off e3. savedHanging / retreatedToSafety needs a before-vs-after SEE check plus 'this move added a defender or moved the hanging unit.' False rescues are worse than silence because I will stare at the board looking for a capture that does not exist.

suggestions.title: Never print strongest/playable with no because
suggestions.detail: c3, g3, a6, h6, e4, f5, Be2, g4, a3: verdict and stop. pickBenefitReasons drops generics, then describeBecause returns null. If nothing concrete survives, keep one generic (center_control/development) or a new pawn_break / prophylaxis slot rather than an empty strongest. Missed_improvement must require a suggestedBecause; 'but g4 would be better.' is how learners mute the mascot.

suggestions.title: Name pawn files in attacker lists
suggestions.detail: labeledPiece skips squares for pawns, so attackerPhrase renders 'the white pawn and pawn' on ...d4. Use the file ('the c-pawn and e-pawn') the same way knights get squares. This is a one-function fix and it is the difference between a hanging-pawn lesson and a glitch.

suggestions.title: Do not call a 40cp drop the strongest move
suggestions.detail: classifyPlayedMove returns best whenever played UCI equals bestMoveUci, and this dump (Lichess omits `best` on unannotated plies) therefore stamps e3, a6, Nd2 (51cp) as best. Margin is null with one PV, so templates never use 'one of several strong moves.' If margin is null or evalLossCp > 0, do not emit 'the strongest move'; use good/excellent copy or near_equal wording. The override should not outrank a 50cp loss.

suggestions.title: Add pawn-break and opposite-castle reasons
suggestions.detail: ...e4, ...f5, and 2.d4 are breaks; O-O vs O-O-O is an attacking race. None of that exists as a reason kind, so the coach falls back to center_control or concatenates castle + semi_open_file into a run-on. A pawn_break fact (pawn move that contacts an enemy center pawn) and an opposite_side_castle flag, with phrase-bank lines, would hit this game four times and most club games once. Include check as a second because when wins_material is also check (Bxh7+).

whatWorked: ...Re8: actually named the pin of the e-pawn to the queen.
13.c4: pawn-shield copy is the rare structural lesson that matches the board.
...fxe4 vs Nb4: hanging recapture plus a named bishop-and-queen fork.
Bxe4: recapture plus the discovered rook hit (even if 'the black pawn' should have been d4).
...Qf6 / Rxe4: hanging knight, ignored threat, and a recapture that saves it — this is the coaching the rest of the game owed me.
Kingside castle: king out of danger and rook in, which is the one stock line I will accept.
